races.name: Racedays For 9 Pound At Nottingham Racecourse Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cosmic Mystery
runners_data.comment: Undersized but sprint-bred and sharp, rated the best of this quintet on 82, she should take a real step forward once she gets a second completed run under her, having unseated at Redcar last time. Effective at 5f, and today's faster ground suits her ideally. The yard is without a winner from 31 runners in the last fortnight, but she looks clear of this field on the balance of the facts.

runners_data.name: Glamorize
runners_data.comment: Below her best when beaten 9 1/4 lengths in a Group 3 at Ascot last time, plainly out of her depth in that grade, but drops back appreciably today and wears cheekpieces for the first time. Effective at 5f on quick ground, with the yard among the in-form stables currently. Rates a leading threat back at a suitable level.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.comment: Green and never able to land a blow on his only start, a well-beaten eighth in a novice at Windsor last time. He's bred for speed and there should be more to come with that experience now banked, but he needs it given the modest form shown so far. Rated bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: One In A Millz
runners_data.comment: Stepped forward from his debut when beaten 9 lengths in a novice at this course last time, though the form was still modest, and there's plenty more needed to be competitive here. Bred for speed and open to more with racing experience, but the yard is out of form currently at just 4% over the last fortnight. Rated a workable contender rather than a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.comment: This colt changed hands for £5,000 as a juvenile and is bred for speed - by the smart sprinter Showcasing out of Dutch Treat, herself a useful sprinter, with a half-brother in Perfect Spring who was useful at 6f. This yard isn't renowned for first-time winners, but he looks sharp enough for 5f. Untested, with plenty still to find out.

races.name: Ivor Thirst Sprint Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mariselle
runners_data.comment: Her debut at Lingfield was full of promise - travelling strongly into the race before fading late to fourth, beaten 7 1/4 lengths, and she looked to have grasped the basics quickly. With that experience banked there should be more to come, and she's proven over today's trip and goes well on good ground. Rated a leading threat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Miracleoftheandes
runners_data.comment: Sent off well fancied for her second start, she set a strong pace at Newbury before weakening out of contention late, fourth beaten 7 lengths. That was almost a year ago and she'll need to progress to figure again, but she is proven over today's trip and ground. A modest profile that leaves her with plenty to prove back after a long spell off.

runners_data.name: Shego
runners_data.comment: An unraced daughter of Eqtidaar out of a mare who was useful at 7f at two but without a win of her own, and with the yard among the in-form stables currently. This experience alone may be what she needs before she shows her best. Rated highly on our figures, but she remains unproven in a race environment.

runners_data.name: Sugar Bon Bon
runners_data.comment: Race keen and never landed a blow when well beaten in a novice at Catterick latest, with the figures (8th, 5th) pointing to a horse who needs more to find. Bred for more of a test than today's minimum trip offers, which is unlikely to play to his strengths. Rated near the foot of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Tide Runner
runners_data.comment: Forced to switch and short of a change of gear when well beaten in a maiden at Ayr latest, with the soft ground possibly not helping his cause. A quicker surface today should suit, given he acts on sound going and is proven at this minimum trip. Recent figures (7th, 3rd) still leave plenty to find, and he's rated only a place chance.

runners_data.name: Courageous Sioux
runners_data.comment: Struggling for pace and green early on her debut at Thirsk, this filly was some way off it before finishing well enough once she began to travel, beaten 5 lengths. That experience should help, especially with this yard renowned for sharpening horses for a second start, and she returns from a long absence but is proven over today's trip. Rated a leading threat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Court Alert
runners_data.comment: Useful at two but inconsistent since, and the four-length fourth at Brighton latest carries an excuse - denied a clear run, he had little left in space, understandable in just his second start back from wind surgery. Drops to the minimum trip on quick ground, and more to come. Winless in five, but rated the one to beat.

runners_data.name: El Ghuwah
runners_data.comment: Unraced newcomer, a 1,000gns Mohaather gelding whose family carries residual promise - half-brother Gordon Norse was useful at 7f and successful second time out. With no form of his own, the market may be the best guide on debut, and this looks stiff company to open in. Rated only a fringe player.

runners_data.name: Green Champion
runners_data.comment: A well-related newcomer by the sprint influence Mehmas out of the smart sprinter Lady Of The Desert, and a half-brother to Queen Kindly, useful at 6f. This yard is adept at readying juveniles first time out, and the minimum trip looks his likely metier. Unexposed, with more expected than the figures currently show, but everything to prove.

races.name: Gold Star Gallop Handicap

runners_data.name: Charlie Boyo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's three-year-old has placed twice at five furlongs on good ground this season, but at heart races from the rear — squeezed into a congested midfield pack here, finding a clear run will be harder than his best form suggests and the uncontested pace from Zarinca does him no favours.
runners_data.comment: Missed the break and was ridden hard to make up the deficit in a handicap at Windsor last time, understandably running out of steam to finish well beaten, 8 1/4 lengths back. Once a useful sort at two over the minimum trip on quick ground, he presumably had some issue along the way and has that ability still to confirm. A first-time tongue-tie is fitted, but he's rated bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's filly has one win from nine runs but it came at five furlongs on good ground; she is a natural hold-up performer who will find herself in a crowded mid-division here, and stepping up to six furlongs for the first time in her last five outings is a genuine stamina question on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Conditions at a tight track worked against her last time, beaten 3 lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Goodwood, though the effort was true to her current form. She hasn't been at her sharpest of late and her mark keeps easing, but she's suited by the minimum trip and acts on a range of going, including today's. A leading contender on these figures.

runners_data.name: Macanudo
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' five-year-old has done all his recent racing at seven furlongs on standard Tapeta, so this drop to six furlongs on fast turf is a significant shift in conditions; a hold-up runner whose best performances have come on a surface that suits sustained late running, he looks the most out of place in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Missing the break forced early exertions that left little in reserve, and he faded down the field in a handicap at Southwell most recently, with more needed to be competitive here. He's effective across 5f-7f, but the yard is misfiring badly at present, managing just a single winner from 47 runners in the last fortnight. Rated an each-way player at best.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: Richard Fahey's two-year-old returns from a 351-day absence, which is the single biggest concern in the race regardless of style; she has shown glimpses over six furlongs on good ground but juvenile absence rust on this going, combined with a natural off-the-pace style, makes her hard to rely upon here.
runners_data.comment: A well below-par effort in a handicap at Haydock last time, beaten 7 1/4 lengths and never landing a blow, is the most recent evidence, and there have evidently been underlying issues since. Nearly a year off the track now, she may be worth simply monitoring rather than backing on this return, though she is proven over today's trip and going. Winless in four, with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: George Scott's three-year-old has a win and a second in recent form and is the highest-rated genuine hold-up horse in the field; his best effort came at six furlongs on soft ground, and the step onto faster terrain with Rowan Scott aboard is worth monitoring, though his form string suggests he runs honestly when conditions suit.
runners_data.comment: Back down in trip suited him last time, and he progressed again to be beaten only a neck off a 2lb lower mark at Windsor, continuing an upward curve that includes a win earlier in the sequence. A promising sort whose breathing issue looks to have been resolved, he's effective at 6f and stretches out well to 7f, with the yard among the in-form stables. Rated clear of this field and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — Edward Bethell's three-year-old won over six furlongs on standard going last time and has not been headed early in recent starts; Paul Mulrennan takes over in the saddle and a clear lead on fast ground with no pace rival in the field gives this horse the optimal conditions to control and potentially outstay the field.
runners_data.comment: A handicap debut at Pontefract came too soon after a break, and she paid for it late on, beaten 6 lengths, though that experience should bring improvement now. She already has a win under her belt this term, but remains unproven on turf having made her mark on the all-weather so far. Effective at 6f, and unexposed enough to progress from here.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's seven-year-old is the most course-and-distance-consistent horse in the race with three wins at six furlongs on good ground from fifteen attempts; David Nolan keeps the ride, the headgear flag points to a prominent tracking role, and his profile as a horse who has won fresh and races handily makes him the most credible threat to Zarinca.
runners_data.comment: A winner of this race twelve months ago, and successful by a half-length off the same mark at Thirsk in May, he's since held his form without adding to that tally, running to par in sixth, beaten 2 lengths, off 75 last time. First-time cheekpieces go on, and he's effective at 5f-6f on any going. The mark now asks more, but he's a leading player.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's five-year-old won over this course, distance and going combination in recent form and carries top weight of 140lbs; a natural hold-up performer whose trainer has had no winners from 14 runners in the last fortnight, he will need either a strong pace or a gap to open late — neither is guaranteed in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Successful by a head off a 5lb lower mark at Wolverhampton two starts back, he's continued that upward curve, running to form again when second, beaten just a half-length, off 1lb less than he carries today. Full of confidence on his last couple of starts and race-fit over course and distance, he wears both a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time. Effective at 6f on any ground, he holds obvious claims off what looks a fair mark.

races.paceDynamic: Zarinca is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Paul Mulrennan can control the tempo from the front at whatever clip suits, making this a strongly front-runner-biased race shape over Nottingham's straight six. The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions for the 7:00 race, which rewards horses that travel cleanly and hold their position rather than those who need a strong gallop to reel in leaders. The bulk of the remainder — Charlie Boyo, Duskaura, Beyond Borders, Eartha, Macanudo and Acclaimed Freedom — are all catalogued as hold-up types, meaning the midfield and rear will be congested and none of them are likely to get the truly soft lead they would need to make their finishing kick count. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse on the front end and any horse with genuine prominent-racing ability; a lone, uncontested leader on fast ground over six furlongs with a wall of hold-up horses behind is a classic profile for a front-runner to outstay the field. The field holds significantly more genuine hold-up horses than can all find their natural rear position — Charlie Boyo, Duskaura, Eartha, Macanudo and Beyond Borders are all true closers compressed into a group, with Zarinca most certain to secure the uncontested lead and Emperor Caradoc, whose headgear flag suggests a prominent or chasing role, best placed to track and challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zarinca Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca jumps cleanly and Mulrennan dictates a comfortable, controlling tempo from the front with no horse willing or able to press.
scenarios.body: If Zarinca jumps cleanly and Mulrennan dictates a comfortable, controlling tempo from the front with no horse willing or able to press.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca goes hard early or the pace proves genuinely strong enough to collapse in the final furlong, opening a late lane for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: If Zarinca goes hard early or the pace proves genuinely strong enough to collapse in the final furlong, opening a late lane for the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Emperor Caradoc Stalks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Emperor Caradoc tracks Zarinca in second or third throughout and produces a sustained challenge from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: If Emperor Caradoc tracks Zarinca in second or third throughout and produces a sustained challenge from the two-furlong pole.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Competitive Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the congested hold-up group creates interference, the pace proves uneven, and no single horse asserts cleanly.
scenarios.body: If the congested hold-up group creates interference, the pace proves uneven, and no single horse asserts cleanly.

watchPoints.text: Zarinca's jumping and first two furlongs are critical — if Mulrennan is allowed to slot in at the front unchallenged before the two-furlong marker, the race may already be won; any drift or sluggish break removes his entire tactical advantage.

Beyond Borders carries top weight on a course and distance he has won over before, but the trainer's 0-for-14 form in the last 14 days is a live concern — watch the market to see whether stable confidence is reflected in his price movement.

Emperor Caradoc's position in the first furlong will define whether Scenario C becomes live — if he tracks Zarinca within two lengths, his good-ground course record makes him a genuine danger; if he gets shuffled back into the hold-up pack, his chance diminishes sharply.

Eartha's 351-day absence for a two-year-old stepping back into a handicap company on fast ground warrants caution — watch how she moves in the market and whether Fahey has given any public indication she is ready to run to her best on return.

The congestion of five or more genuine hold-up horses compressed into the middle and rear creates a traffic risk in the final two furlongs — any horse drawn widest or with a jockey willing to switch wide early (particularly Acclaimed Freedom with Rowan Scott) may get first run on the outside.

races.name: Nottingham's Finest Ale Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here and handed a gift lead on Good to Firm — his 1W3P record at similar going is encouraging, and Rowan Scott has a clear tactical brief to conserve energy on a lone lead over this 1m6f trip; STYLE_FIT tag means he is technically operating at the edge of his comfort zone at this distance, so stamina late is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Won by four lengths at Lingfield last time, stepping up in trip to beat an in-form rival for a yard that's firing, and he's only risen 6lb for it. Stays this two-mile trip, handles good ground, and rates the one to beat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Saratoga Gold
runners_data.note: Best form profile at this trip, with multiple places at 1m6f and 1m4f on similar going (0W4P at sim-going suggests consistency without winning, but involvement is reliable); William Pyle's booking is straightforward and at 8 years old this horse knows its job off a 24-day break.
runners_data.comment: A keen-going sort well beaten in a Kempton handicap last time after over-racing, undoing a run of closer efforts; first-time blinkers may settle him. Winless in five starts but proven over today's trip and ground, he'd take plenty of catching back on that better form.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Trainer Ian Williams is 4/36 over the last 14 days (active yard), but Free World's own recent form is a serious concern — five consecutive out-of-the-money finishes on Good and the prominent ⚠ fade tag suggest a horse that does not see out its races; mapped to midfield rather than its natural rear position because the hold-up group is oversized, which compounds its tactical problem.
runners_data.comment: Struggled up in trip when beaten nine lengths in a Sandown handicap last time, and this new yard has little to go on beyond a flash of promise in Meydan, leaving him with plenty to find off this mark. Suited around today's trip, but with just one modest placing from four runs, he's hard to trust on figures.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: Returns from a 309-day absence (53 jumps runs last seen) which is a significant flag — visored for concentration, and while it has Good to Good Firm form at a distance (2W5P at sim-going), the very long layoff and the step back from extreme NH trips means fitness is the critical unknown for David Nolan.
runners_data.comment: A dual-purpose sort who raced up with the pace and worked hard through the first half before being pulled up in a hurdles handicap at Hereford last time, form easily forgiven. First-time visor and a workable mark on his hurdling form add appeal, and he's proven over today's trip and ground off a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Chambers
runners_data.note: Off 222 days (31 jump runs), Tom Eaves takes the ride but the form string of 40457 in flat handicaps at this sort of trip shows no recent impact — genuinely a hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is compromised by the depth of the hold-up division in this field, dulling its prospects regardless of pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Continuing an inconsistent run across both codes, he never travelled and looked green when well beaten in a Warwick maiden hurdle latest. Best form has come at shorter trips on the all-weather, and without a win in five he's hard to fancy over today's stiffer 14f test.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Ben Case's runner sports a hood and returns from 33 days off, showing some recent placed form (2W3P at similar going) at this type of trip; in reality a true hold-up operator whose best chances come when pace is strong enough to reel in, but the uncontested lead scenario this race presents is structurally unfavourable for her needs.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time cheekpieces, she was successful in this same contest a year ago and already boasts course, trip and today's ground form. Below her best this season and beaten seven lengths at Windsor last time without excuse, she nonetheless remains capable of running well again today.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, he should stride into a comfortable, uncontested position from the jump and control the tempo over this 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham. Behind him, the field is stacked with hold-up types — Saratoga Gold, Ikigai Star, Chambers, Free World, and Regally Blonde — meaning the mid-to-rear section will be congested and tactical positioning will be restricted. Three of those hold-up runners (Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde) have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the true rear is overcrowded, but they are not natural prominent racers and their positional shuffle creates a muddled mid-pack rather than genuine pace competition. This shape overwhelmingly favours a horse capable of travelling strongly in the slipstream of a lone, measured front-runner and producing a sustained, rather than explosive, finishing effort — a strong traveller who can pick up from just off the pace is best positioned, while pure hold-up horses who need a fast tempo to generate their run are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Langley Controls, Closer Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley dictates an honest but unhurried gallop and the hold-up runners have enough time to organise late runs from a compact midfield.
scenarios.body: If Jack Langley dictates an honest but unhurried gallop and the hold-up runners have enough time to organise late runs from a compact midfield.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Langley Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses fail to organise a sustained challenge and Langley's pace judgment leaves the field flat-footed turning for home.
scenarios.body: If the hold-up horses fail to organise a sustained challenge and Langley's pace judgment leaves the field flat-footed turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Midfield Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Regally Blonde or Chambers, shuffled into midfield despite being true hold-up types, manage to find a prominent position early and time their challenge better than the true deep closers.
scenarios.body: If Regally Blonde or Chambers, shuffled into midfield despite being true hold-up types, manage to find a prominent position early and time their challenge better than the true deep closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Deep Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Langley goes faster than expected in the early stages and weakens dramatically in the final quarter mile, freeing the deep hold-up types to come from well off the pace.
scenarios.body: If Langley goes faster than expected in the early stages and weakens dramatically in the final quarter mile, freeing the deep hold-up types to come from well off the pace.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Jack Langley is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first half mile — if Rowan Scott dictates a very slow tempo, the race becomes a sprint for home and his stamina limitations late become irrelevant.

Ikigai Star's 309-day absence (last seen in jump company) means fitness is genuinely unverifiable — David Nolan may educate this horse rather than ride it for maximum effect, and punters should treat it accordingly.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde) are likely to crowd each other in the middle of the field with no natural prominent runner to follow — watch for traffic and interference in the straight as they all seek the same ground simultaneously.

Free World's ⚠ fade flag and five consecutive poor finishes on Good ground make it a horse to watch fade rather than finish — if it briefly threatens turning in, expect it to be swallowed up inside the final furlong.

Saratoga Gold's trainer Kevin & Lauren Frost are 3/17 in the last 14 days — a stable showing reasonable recent form — and the 24-day break for an 8-year-old who has placed four times at similar going suggests a straightforward each-way contender, not a speculative one.

races.name: Shipstones 1852 Heritage Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Celestias Comet
runners_data.note: Fanshawe-trained hold-up filly who has struggled for consistency (form 0-6655) but her best effort came on Good ground and she handles this trip — drawn to benefit from Scenario A if she can reproduce her similar-going placed effort.|
runners_data.comment: A modest run of five without a win includes a comfortable defeat back on turf at Brighton last time, beaten 6 lengths in a handicap, and there's more needed on this evidence. Her mark keeps drifting the right way, though, and the yard is among the in-form stables, while a first-time hood may add a touch of sharpness. Effective around today's trip on quick ground, but others hold stronger claims on figures.

runners_data.name: Phaedra
runners_data.note: Strong recent form on Good going (2nd twice in last five), best at 10f-12f, and Joey Ramsden's yard has had one winner from ten runners in the past 14 days — genuine closer whose historical record of three wins and four places on similar going makes her the most compelling beneficiary of a run-to-finish shape.|
runners_data.comment: Frequently in the frame without going one better across six runs, this filly bounced back into form when fitted with a first-time tongue-tie last time, keeping on for a 3-length defeat at Doncaster off the same mark she carries today. She raced free but the headgear evidently helped settle her, and she is suited by this longer trip on a sound surface. A workable mark and clear claims among the principals.

runners_data.name: Huggable
runners_data.note: Won once and placed twice from ten attempts on similar ground but her 0.91 style-fit score reflects that she is a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot in a field where the rear is already full — her chance hinges on whether she can settle close enough to produce her usual finishing kick without being blocked.|
runners_data.comment: Still to hit form this campaign, and stepping up in trip did her no favours when down the field in a handicap at Salisbury last time. She's better suited back around 10f, with soft ground bringing out her best, though the yard is out of form currently at just 3% over the last fortnight. Others look to hold stronger claims on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Tagged as the redistributed pace-setter despite a natural tendency to race from behind, her style-fit of 0.80 is the lowest in the field — she becomes the accidental front-runner by elimination but there is a genuine risk she either idles in front or is unable to hold her lead when the closers arrive.|
runners_data.comment: An inconsistent sort who nonetheless has looked a big player two runs back, this filly gets cheekpieces for the first time today after a moderate effort down the field in a handicap at Wolverhampton last time. She is suited by this longer trip on a sound surface, and the headgear could be the key to unlocking her best. Winless in five, but rated clear of this field on figures.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Carries a notable finish-fade flag from her form record, which is a significant concern in a race likely to develop into a test of late stamina on fast ground; Tim Easterby's yard is in solid recent form (14 winners from 112 runners in 14 days), but her natural hold-up style is squeezed into a crowded midfield and her tendency to weaken late limits her appeal.|
runners_data.comment: Questions remain over whether she truly stays this sort of trip, and a below-par effort in a handicap at Musselburgh last time, beaten 5 lengths, may have owed something to that. Best form has come around a mile on a sound surface, and she wears a hood for the first time today. Unreliable but clearly capable on her figures, and rates a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's filly drops sharply in class at OR=49 and recorded a recent win over 8f at Sandown, though all four of her turf runs on Good ground produced modest results (7th, 7th, 4th) — she is a true hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution, and her chance depends on the pace genuinely lifting in the final quarter-mile.|
runners_data.comment: Won by a half-length off a 2lb lower mark at Newcastle two starts back, and clearly in good order round then, this filly ran into trouble at a vital stage when fourth last time, beaten 5 lengths off the same mark she carries today. She is effective around a mile and on softer ground, with the all-weather having proven tougher for her. Rated bottom of this field but not without recent claims.

races.paceDynamic: Saliko is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field, redistributed to the lead from a hold-up tag, and on Good to Firm ground at Nottingham will likely set a measured, uncontested gallop over 1m2f with no rival prepared to push the tempo from outside. With just one horse controlling fractions, the race will almost certainly be run at a sustainable pace through the early stages, with the field strung loosely behind before the tempo picks up in the straight. That controlled shape favours hold-up horses who can finish powerfully through a strong gallop — the kind of race where a true closer hitting the line late is rewarded. However, this field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate: Huggable, Rosemary May, and Dinah Myte are all genuine hold-up horses compressed into a midfield slot, meaning several runners will be racing out of their natural position and may struggle to produce a clean finish from far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saliko Controls, Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko sets an honest but sustainable pace unchallenged and the race develops into a test of finishing power in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Saliko sets an honest but sustainable pace unchallenged and the race develops into a test of finishing power in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Saliko Gifts It
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko's redistribution from hold-up to lead proves artificial and the gallop is so slow that the leader simply steals it without being challenged.
scenarios.body: If Saliko's redistribution from hold-up to lead proves artificial and the gallop is so slow that the leader simply steals it without being challenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Bottleneck Punishes Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of hold-up types causes traffic issues and interference in the straight, disrupting the late runs of the horses mapped out of position.
scenarios.body: If the surplus of hold-up types causes traffic issues and interference in the straight, disrupting the late runs of the horses mapped out of position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dinah Myte Improves Sharply
scenarios.trigger: If Dinah Myte's recent course-and-distance form (4th on Good at 8f) combines with a drop in class and a hot pace to spring an upset.
scenarios.body: If Dinah Myte's recent course-and-distance form (4th on Good at 8f) combines with a drop in class and a hot pace to spring an upset.

watchPoints.text: Phaedra is 8 days fresh off a run and carries strong recent form at this trip — watch whether Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) positions her early enough to avoid the hold-up traffic bottleneck in the straight.

Saliko is the accidental front-runner and her style-fit of 0.80 flags this is not her natural role — if she idles or drifts in the lead on Good to Firm, watch for the field bunching dangerously at the two-furlong pole.

Rosemary May carries an explicit finish-fade flag — if Rhys Elliott (5lb claimer) fails to get her into a prominent enough position given her hold-up redistribution, she risks being swamped before the line and becoming a significant non-factor.

Dinah Myte is the biggest class dropper in the race and represents Gallagher's yard hitting form (2 from 6 in 14 days) — if she breaks well and is allowed to creep into contention naturally rather than being dropped out, she could outrun her outside price.

races.name: Last Orders Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Nigel Tinkler who has placed at 8f on good ground (2/5 sim-going), now stepping up to 1m2f which looks a positive move; sits just off the pace and may find the extra distance suits him well enough to chase the leader home.
runners_data.comment: Needs to bounce back after a below-par run at Wetherby latest, beaten six and a quarter lengths, with the yard also out of form currently. He does act on quick ground at today's trip, so he's not without claims, but the case for him goes only so far on these figures.

runners_data.name: Regulus Black
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old won over 10f on good going 17 days ago and carries a STYLE_FIT flag as a prominent type confirmed to lead today — his ability to control fractions unchallenged is the dominant tactical factor in this race, and his recent course-trip-going form reads best of all.
runners_data.comment: Won by two lengths at Chepstow two starts back and confirmed that promise when third, beaten just two lengths, up in trip last time on an unchanged mark. Now handicapping over middle distances with the yard in good form, he remains on a fair mark and rates the one to beat, even if he still needs to find that little extra to land this.

runners_data.name: Palace Artois
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends this hold-up type back out after just 12 days, wearing headgear, but a sequence of finishes in the 5th-7th range at 8f suggests the trip-up to 1m2f may unlock improvement; his natural rear-of-field style will require a stronger gallop than Regulus Black may supply.
runners_data.comment: Undone for speed when beaten ten lengths in a Windsor handicap last time, but that run came at a shorter trip than ideal and today's step up should suit her finishing pace. First-time cheekpieces add further interest and she's proven on this going, though she needs to find plenty more than she's shown to be involved.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly has run only three times, all at 8f, with a best effort of 7th — stepping up in trip after 26 days off, and although she is a true hold-up type, the race map places her in midfield as genuine closers are oversubscribed; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence she can reproduce hold-up form from that position.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a novice at Windsor latest under a stiffer test than she was ready for, but she's bred to appreciate more of a stamina test now handicapping. Form is sparse from just three starts, though improvement looks likely at this longer trip, and she remains of interest on a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Baldosa
runners_data.note: Two placings over 10f on comparable ground give Baldosa the strongest trip-profile of the hold-up contingent, and he and stablemate Balmoral Boy represent Nigel Tinkler, whose 14-day record is modest (0/21); mapped to midfield despite being a natural hold-up runner because of field congestion at the rear — needs the pace to be honest.
runners_data.comment: A maiden yet to get her head in front, but her form's plainly on the up, matching her true level when beaten just two lengths off an unchanged mark in a handicap at Wetherby last time. Proven over today's trip and going, she remains of interest for a leading threat, even with the yard currently out of winners.

runners_data.name: Alcanzor
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner carries a noted tendency to fade in the finish, arrives after a 54-day break, and has run only three times — all at shorter trips (7-8f) — making the 1m2f a question mark; held up naturally but the map redistribution means he won't get his true trailing position, compounding the stamina query.
runners_data.comment: Down the field again without ever threatening in a novice at Catterick most recent, and with only three starts to his name the boost from stepping up in trip has yet to be tested. He's bred to be suited by today's longer distance, but on what he's shown he needs to progress plenty before he can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Enduring Story
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's consistent finisher has run six times this season, placing repeatedly in the 5th-9th bracket at 7f for William Pyle, and the step to 1m2f is unproven; like several others here, his true hold-up style is compressed into a midfield slot by the field composition, making a winning run dependent on unusually strong late acceleration.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten again in a handicap at Redcar latest, extending a run of poor form that's yet to show any encouragement, and the yard is similarly out of touch currently. Rock-bottom on our figures, she has plenty to prove before being taken seriously.

races.paceDynamic: Regulus Black is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m2f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground from the outset. The remainder of the field — Balmoral Boy, Palace Artois, Sound Gloria, Baldosa, Alcanzor, and Enduring Story — are all hold-up or midfield types, meaning the pace is entirely in Regulus Black's hands and is unlikely to be truly searching. Crucially, Sound Gloria, Baldosa, Alcanzor, and Enduring Story are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there is simply no room for multiple true closers at the rear in a field this small — Regulus Black and, to the extent they push forward, Balmoral Boy and Palace Artois are most likely to actually secure a forward position. A steadily-run mile-and-two in which Regulus Black can bowl along unhurried will compress the field into a bunch and make it very hard for hold-up runners to find the gaps they need late — this race shape strongly favours the prominent-racing profile, and any hold-up horse will need an unusually strong late surge to overcome a front-runner who has never been asked to quicken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regulus Black Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Regulus Black is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and sets a measured pace, controlling the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: If Regulus Black is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and sets a measured pace, controlling the tempo throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battles It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Palace Artois or Balmoral Boy push forward to press Regulus Black more than expected, injecting enough pace to set up a genuine contest.
scenarios.body: If Palace Artois or Balmoral Boy push forward to press Regulus Black more than expected, injecting enough pace to set up a genuine contest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves fast enough to stretch the field and a true closer can find a clear run from midfield in the home straight.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves fast enough to stretch the field and a true closer can find a clear run from midfield in the home straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Finish, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the race degenerates into a sprint from two furlongs out with no single horse in control.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses entirely and the race degenerates into a sprint from two furlongs out with no single horse in control.

watchPoints.text: Regulus Black's lead is completely uncontested — if Ross Coakley is able to dictate fully, the pace will be so controlled that hold-up horses waiting for a quickening move will simply have no injection of pace to latch onto.

Baldosa and Sound Gloria are natural hold-up horses but will not get that position today — watch early for whether either jockey tries to settle them at the rear anyway, which could leave them with a near-impossible task from a false rearward berth in a slow-run race.

Alcanzor's 54-day absence combined with a tendency to fade in the finish is a significant risk in a race that will likely test stamina at 1m2f — watch for signs of him weakening sharply from the two-furlong pole.

Palace Artois reappears after just 12 days wearing headgear — watch at the start to see whether Mulrennan pushes forward earlier than expected, as any move to press Regulus Black would be the key trigger for Scenario B materialising.

The going report consistently shows Good to Firm at 1m2f across multiple readings at Nottingham tonight — horses with confirmed good-ground form (Regulus Black, Baldosa's 4th over 10f on good) hold a surface advantage over those whose recent outings came on soft or standard.

races.name: Construction Day 14th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with placed form on good ground at 8-10f but disappointing recent figures (form 983-67); Jake Dickson's 7lb claim softens the weight to 135lbs, though the horse's sim-going record (0 wins, 2 places from 9 on similar) suggests consistency is lacking at this level.
runners_data.comment: A long-time maiden whose mark keeps easing, he wanted more pace to work with when beaten five lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time. The yard's in good form, he's drawn stall two, and first-time cheekpieces could be the change that finally gets him off the mark — he's a leading contender on our figures regardless.

runners_data.name: Holly Mist
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 4yo has placed form at 10-12f and, uniquely in this field, carries an UNKNOWN base style (U), meaning she may adapt tactically — Varian's 9/32 T14 strike rate and Harry Vigors's 5lb claim are positive angles, though sim-going record is thin (1 run, 0W0P).
runners_data.comment: Consistency has been the hallmark of her recent starts, and she matched her true form when beaten just three and a quarter lengths off a 1lb higher mark at Doncaster last time. The trainer's in excellent touch, the mark continues to ease, and first-time blinkers could sharpen her up further at a trip she handles well.

runners_data.name: Time Turner
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's hold-up type won over 12f on soft and placed over 10f on similar ground; the visor is applied and Paul Mulrennan takes the ride, suggesting connections are trying to sharpen his focus after a nine-runner finish last time; trip and going profile align well.
runners_data.comment: A slow-away sort who had too much lost ground to make up when beaten a length and a quarter off a 1lb higher mark at Musselburgh last time, a fair effort back from a break. Generally holds his form and is proven at today's trip and going, but the first-time visor points to early speed as his main issue.

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, which gives Ross Coakley a straightforward tactical brief; Mark Loughnane sends him out cold (0W from 17 in 14-day window) and the horse's style-fit tag (0.93) reflects that uncontested lead-setting is not always his optimal role — his sim-going record (1W3P) shows he can deliver but at a reduced confidence level.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency with three thirds on the spin, his latest Windsor defeat coming only after trouble in running for a rise of just 2lb since. Suited by today's trip and ground, with cheekpieces added for the first time, he rates the one to beat on our figures, even though he had nothing extra to offer once the trouble cleared last time.

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 4yo is a genuine hold-up type displaced into the midfield map position because the rear is oversubscribed; recent form reads 6780-0, flagged as fading in the finish, and the sim-going record (0W0P from 3 runs) does not inspire confidence — the style-fit discount (0.90) is the lowest in the field, meaning this horse is most compromised by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time when outpowered for speed, though that effort may have owed something to needing the run. Solid enough at today's trip and going, but with no big placing efforts in his last five and form that's genuinely hard to assess, he's tough to trust with confidence.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 5yo carries the best recent form of the hold-up contingent (221433) and has five places from seven runs on similar going; shown in midfield on the map because hold-up slots are exhausted, but his class and consistency give him the best chance of the REDISTRIBUTED group if he can work forward into a tracking role.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency with a win and four places from his last six starts, only nudged out late when beaten a length and a half off an unchanged mark at Brighton last time. Effective at today's trip on quick ground, with first-time cheekpieces added, he takes plenty of catching but still needs more to reverse placings with the principals.

runners_data.name: Pride Eye
runners_data.note: A long layoff of 124 days raises a fitness query, and all five recent runs have come on standard Tapeta; the hood is applied and the horse is flagged as fading in the finish — genuine good-to-firm turf form is absent from the record, making going suitability a secondary concern on top of the redistribution out of his natural rear position.
runners_data.comment: Yet to find genuine consistency in a short career, and turf today is new ground after all her starts on the all-weather. Beaten seven and a half lengths at Kempton last time with nothing to blame, and having been off the track for four months, she's hard to fancy despite the first-time tongue-tie offering some change of tactics.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps at the bottom of the weights (120lbs), but form reads 57-097 with a sim-going record of 1W3P from 12 comparable runs — the win came on different ground conditions; one of four true hold-up horses compressed into midfield, and at OR=50 faces the stiffest class ask of the bunch.
runners_data.comment: Forced the pace more than ideal when beaten seven lengths in a Beverley handicap last time, and she's now below the mark that last yielded a win, needing to rediscover that form. Proven at today's trip, but with little consistency across her last five starts, she's hard to trust without more signs of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Stipulation is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control the gallop from the outset over 1m2f on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham. The pace will be sustainable rather than pressured — a single horse setting its own tempo on a flat track creates an honest but not brutal fraction, which typically suits those able to travel in behind and produce a progressive finish. The bulk of this field — Into Combat, Danehill Star, Pride Eye, and Quirke On Parole — are true hold-up horses who cannot all settle naturally at the rear, meaning several will be pushed forward into positions that are not their preferred territory, diluting their finishing kick. This shape favours a prominent or early-tracking profile that can latch onto Stipulation's uncontested gallop and sustain the effort through the final two furlongs, giving a clear advantage to runners like Holly Mist and Danehill Star who can race closer to the pace than their natural style demands.

scenarios.title: Stipulation Controls, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Stipulation sets a sustainable uncontested tempo and a prominent or tracking type travels smoothly into contention from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If Stipulation sets a sustainable uncontested tempo and a prominent or tracking type travels smoothly into contention from the home turn.

scenarios.body: If the sustainable solo gallop is slow enough that Stipulation conserves energy and simply outstays the field from the front.

scenarios.title: Late Kick Materialises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently mid-race that Stipulation ties up in the final furlong and the field fans wide, giving legitimate hold-up runners daylight.
scenarios.body: If the pace quickens sufficiently mid-race that Stipulation ties up in the final furlong and the field fans wide, giving legitimate hold-up runners daylight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Dominant Shape
scenarios.trigger: If several horses contest the early lead or jockeys scramble for position, creating an uneven pace that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If several horses contest the early lead or jockeys scramble for position, creating an uneven pace that scrambles the race shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Stipulation is fully committed to the lead from the off — if Ross Coakley elects to track rather than front-run, the entire pace map collapses and the race becomes genuinely shape-less.

Danehill Star's jockey Tom Eaves will need to make an early decision about where to sit; if he commits to following Stipulation rather than dropping to the rear, Danehill Star becomes a legitimate danger given his good-going form at this trip.

Pride Eye's 124-day absence is a significant fitness flag — if the horse is short of a run, a flattening out in the final furlong would benefit those travelling smoothly in behind, particularly Holly Mist.

Into Combat is flagged as fading in the finish and carries the lowest style-fit score in the race (0.90); if Dylan Hogan pushes forward to secure a better position, watch for that horse to drop away sharply in the final two furlongs, potentially causing interference for runners on the inside.

The going report confirms 1m2f races at Nottingham today are running Good to Firm throughout the card — any horse with a headgear change or fitness concern on quick ground should be monitored in the parade ring for signs of sweat or unease before the off.
